metadata.note: Live Oak, Perry and Gulf Railroad, Florida (Suwannee, Lafayette and Taylor counties): main line Live Oak - Perry (44.0 mi), the Mayo Branch, and the main line west of Perry through Hampton Springs and Waylonzo to Scanlon, with the 1921 extension across the Aucilla to Flint Rock. Eight features: Live Oak - Perry 1906-1956 (the 1952-1956 tail on a single secondary source); Mayo Branch 1906-1951 [OPEN]; Mayo - Alton 1906 [ANCHOR]; Perry - Hampton Springs 1906-1939 [OPEN]; Hampton Springs - Waylonzo 1923 [OPEN] - 1939 [OPEN]; Waylonzo - Scanlon 1939 [ANCHOR]; Waylonzo - Loughridge 1914 [ANCHOR]; Econfena - Flint Rock 1923 [ANCHOR]. NO Rule 4 split: ACL stock control 1918-1928, Brooks-Scanlon ownership 1928/29-1954 and Southern Railway control 1954-1956 were changes of control - the LOP&G ran its own trains under its own name throughout (the 1951 Guide prints its own officers at Perry/Foley). Not drawn: the Murat branch (no passenger evidence), the pre-1906 Dowling log road and Live Oak and Perry RR (no passenger evidence), the South Georgia Railway's through trains Perry - Hampton Springs (another company), the rival Florida Railway Live Oak - Mayo - Perry (another company), and everything after passenger service ended (freight only). Colour #5F8A3C is new to the dataset.
geometry_sources: Nominatim (OSM) geocodes bounded to Suwannee/Lafayette/Taylor counties, FL; Mayo Junction, Foley Junction and Flint Rock hand-pinned
not_yet_sourced: END OF PASSENGER SERVICE: Live Oak - Perry is drawn to 1956 on Tap Lines alone (the 1956 employee-timetable supplement, not seen). Primary/photographic evidence runs to Aug 1951 (Official Guide) and 1952 (dated photo). Worth checking: Suwannee Democrat / Perry Taco Times / Mayo Free Press 1955-56; Florida Railroad and Public Utilities Commission discontinuance orders; Trains magazine 1956.

[OPEN] ends: Mayo Branch (confirmed to Aug 1951 - the system-wide 1956 deletion does not name the branch); Perry - Hampton Springs (confirmed to 1939; ended before Aug 1951, year unknown); Hampton Springs - Waylonzo (confirmed to 1939).
[OPEN] start: Hampton Springs - Waylonzo confirmed only from 1923 though built 1907-1908.
[ANCHOR] single years: Mayo - Alton 1906; Waylonzo - Loughridge 1914; Econfena - Flint Rock 1923; Waylonzo - Scanlon 1939.
Passenger trains before 1906 on Live Oak - Dowling Park - Day (Live Oak and Perry RR from 1903; Dowling log road earlier): plausible, unproven.
The 1917-1932 'motor coach' (Tap Lines) is treated as a rail motor car; if it was a highway bus, rail passenger service in those years needs re-checking.
Fowler shows Murat Junction as the 1929G terminus: whether Murat Jct - Waylonzo lost service c.1929 and regained it by 1939 is unresolved.
Scanlon vs Loughridge (both 64.0 mi): one place renamed or two spurs? Loughridge's geometry is drawn at Scanlon on inference.
Whether LOP&G passenger/mixed trains ran through to Flint Rock over Brooks-Scanlon's last 1.5 mi, or stopped at mp 72.5.
Pre-1930 alignment at Foley Junction - Foley - Perry (Foley appears only from 1939).
source_conflicts: Construction of MP31-MP49 (incl. Perry and Hampton Springs): ICC valuation 1908 vs Fowler's 1906 Official Guide letters and Tap Lines (Perry Feb 1906, Hampton Springs Apr 1906). Drawn from 1906; ICC year taken as completion/accounting.
LOP&G incorporation: ICC 16 Jun 1905 vs Tap Lines 16 Jun 1906 - ICC preferred.
Brooks-Scanlon purchase: Hawkins 1928 vs Taylor County history 1929 - not a split either way.
Motor-car chronology: Tap Lines 1937-1940 doodlebug, mixed from 1940, vs Hawkins' Smalley motorcar #206 acquired 'early 1940s'.
metadata.freight_only_audit: Applied at creation (2026-11-10): no freight-only years drawn. Omitted as freight-only or without passenger evidence: Murat branch; Springdale spur (MP46.5, 1912); Brooks-Scanlon/Burton-Swartz logging spurs; the pre-1906 Dowling log road; all post-1956 operation (Southern, LOP&SG 1971, NS 1994, G&O 1995, Georgia and Florida Railnet).
metadata.horsecar_audit: Not applicable: steam log road from the start; no animal-powered years.

segments.note: Live Oak, Perry and Gulf Railroad (Live Oak and Perry RR inc. 23 Sep 1903; LOP&G inc. 16 Jun 1905 per the ICC valuation, 16 Jun 1906 per Tap Lines - ICC preferred), Live Oak (ACL/SAL union depot) - Starr - Mercer - Newburn - Lancaster - Dowling Park (Suwannee River) - Chancey - Mayo Junction - Day - Townsend - Smith - Fenholloway - Blue Creek (later Foley) Junction - Perry, 44.0 mi. Steam passenger trains from 1906: Tap Lines says the road reached Perry in February 1906, and Fowler's digest of the 1906 Official Guide lists every station Live Oak - Perry. The Live Oak Daily Democrat of 2 May 1907 advertises Sunday trains Live Oak - Dowling Park. SOURCE CONFLICT, recorded: the ICC valuation dates construction MP31-MP49 (which includes Perry) to 1908; two independent sources put trains at Perry in 1906, so the ICC year is taken as a completion/accounting date. The Live Oak - MP31 section existed by Sep 1903 (Live Oak and Perry; earlier the R. L. Dowling log road), but no passenger train before 1906 is proven, so none is drawn. Rival service: the Florida Railway ran Live Oak - Mayo - Perry until 1916 (a separate company, not drawn here). Headway 720 min (two trains each way) is an ESTIMATE - no pre-1923 frequency was read.
sources: Segment-level: start from Fowler's 1906G letters (section 87) and Tap Lines ('built on to Perry (February of 1906)'); 1907 service from the Live Oak Daily Democrat 2 May 1907 p5; ICC construction table for the 1908 conflict; Hawkins for the 1903 MP31 railhead - as read in research/branches/live_oak_perry_and_gulf_railroad.txt (researched 2026-11-10); the tracer did not re-open these sources.

segments.note: Tap Lines: traffic rose after the rival Florida Railway quit in 1916, then 'declining passengers led to the use of a motor coach on the line from 1917 to 1932'. Taken as a RAIL motor car (ECB describes a 'doodlebug ... self-propelled rail car' bought used from the Tampa and Jacksonville; Hawkins records a Smalley rail motorcar), but no source states it outright - if it was a highway bus, rail passenger service in these years would need re-checking. Fowler's 1923 Official Guide letters list the stations. Atlantic Coast Line held stock control 1918-1928 and Brooks-Scanlon bought the road in 1928 (Hawkins) or 1929 (Taylor County history); both were changes of control only - the LOP&G kept running its own trains, so no Rule 4 split. Headway 720 min is an ESTIMATE.
sources: Segment-level: Tap Lines (1916 rise; 1917-1932 motor coach); Fowler 1923G letters; ECB and Hawkins for the motor-car identification; Hawkins/Taylor for the control changes - as read in research/branches/live_oak_perry_and_gulf_railroad.txt (researched 2026-11-10); the tracer did not re-open these sources.

segments.note: Mixed trains from 1932 (Tap Lines), a new doodlebug 1937-1940, mixed trains again from 1940 (Hawkins: in June 1940 'No. 1, the morning mixed train from Live Oak to Perry, returning to Live Oak as No. 2'). Fowler's 1939 and 1947 Official Guide letters list the stations, with Foley (41.0) from 1939. The August 1951 Official Guide (Feb 1952 edition) prints mixed trains Nos. 1-4, two round trips daily except Sunday, with legible times: No.1 Mayo Jct 6:19, Foley Jct 6:58, Foley 7:23, arr Perry 7:33 AM; No.2 lv Perry 8:18 AM, arr Live Oak 11:38 AM; No.4 lv Perry 4:33 PM, arr Live Oak 6:46 PM. Fenholloway is daggered freight-only in that Guide's index - a flag stop dropped, not the line. Headway 600 min is an ESTIMATE from the two 1951 round trips.
sources: Segment-level: Tap Lines (1932 mixed, 1937-1940 doodlebug); Hawkins (June 1940 operation); Fowler 1939G/1947G letters; Official Guide Aug 1951 LOP&G table and Index of Stations (research/sources/official_guide_1952.txt, Guide p.618) - as read in research/branches/live_oak_perry_and_gulf_railroad.txt (researched 2026-11-10); the tracer did not re-open these sources.

segments.note: SINGLE SECONDARY SOURCE. A dated 1952 photograph shows a 'Jim Crow' combine on the back of an LOP&G mixed train (Tap Lines LOPG4). The 1956 end rests on Tap Lines alone: 'the mixed trains were deleted from the timetable in 1956, at which time all trains were ran as extras', the 1956 employee-timetable supplement having 'listed no trains and mentioned that passenger service was no longer offered'. That supplement was not seen, and no month is given. A reader requiring a primary document would stop this line at 1952 [OPEN]. Southern Railway bought control of the LOP&G (and the South Georgia) from Brooks-Scanlon in 1954 and 'operated them as a shortline' - the LOP&G remained the operating company, so the 1954-1956 tail is not split into Southern's colour (caller decision, following the research report's recommendation). Freight continued: Live Oak, Perry and South Georgia 1971, Norfolk Southern 1994, Gulf and Ohio 1995, Georgia and Florida Railnet. Headway 600 min is the 1951 figure carried forward - an ESTIMATE.
sources: Segment-level: SINGLE SECONDARY SOURCE - Tap Lines LOPG4 (1952 photo) and LOPG5/LOPG1 (1956 timetable deletion, citing the 1956 employee-timetable supplement); Taylor County history and Tap Lines for the 1954 Southern purchase - as read in research/branches/live_oak_perry_and_gulf_railroad.txt (researched 2026-11-10); the tracer did not re-open these sources.

segments.note: Mayo Branch, Mayo Junction - Dell (Clark in 1906) - Peterson - Mayo, seat of Lafayette County, 12.0 mi. Built 1906 as part of Mayo Jct - Alton (ICC, 14.53 mi); Tap Lines dates the branch opening to April 1906; Fowler's 1906G letters list Peterson and Mayo (1906 trains ran on to Alton - see the Mayo - Alton feature), and Mayo is the terminus in 1923, 1939 and 1947. Hawkins records a Mayo Jct - Mayo mixed in June 1940; Tap Lines has a 1948 photo of the mixed switching the branch; the August 1951 Official Guide table 'LIVE OAK AND MAYO' prints Mixed No.5 Mayo Jct 9:22 - Dell 9:36 - Peterson 9:46 - arr Mayo 9:58 AM and No.6 back to Live Oak 11:38 AM. [OPEN] END: passenger service on the branch is confirmed to Aug 1951. This is the last CONFIRMED year, not a known end - Tap Lines' 1956 deletion of the mixed trains is system-wide and does not name the branch, which could have lost its mixed earlier. Do not extend without evidence. Not to be confused with the Florida Railway's separate Stokely Jct - Mayo line (opened 1902, ended 1916). Headway 1440 min (one round trip daily) is the 1951 figure applied to every era - an ESTIMATE.

segments.note: Perry - Springdale - Pershing - Hampton Springs, the LOP&G main line west of Perry to the Hampton Springs sulphur-spring resort (Hotel Hampton, burned 1954). Opened April 1906 (Tap Lines); Fowler's 1906G letters show Hampton Springs as the terminus, and it is listed again in 1923 and 1939. SOURCE CONFLICT, recorded: the ICC valuation dates MP31-MP49 to 1908 (see Live Oak - Perry). In 1923 South Georgia Railway trains also ran through Perry to Hampton Springs over this track (Fowler section 99) - a separate company, not drawn in this layer. [OPEN] END: passenger service is confirmed to 1939 by the 1939 Official Guide (via Fowler). This is the last CONFIRMED year, not a known end - Hampton Springs is absent from the 1947 list, which is not evidence of an end, and by Aug 1951 the row at 47.0 mi (Springdale) sits under the Guide's 'Freight service only' footnote, so passengers stopped at an unknown year between 1939 and 1951. Do not extend without evidence. Headway 720 min is an ESTIMATE.

Built 1921 (Tap Lines: Flint Rock reached 1921, 74 mi from Live Oak; LOP&G end of line at mp 72.5, the final 1.5 mi owned by Brooks-Scanlon). ONE proven year: Mandalay and Flint Rock appear only in Fowler's digest of the 1923 Official Guide.
